text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told reporters between sessions of the National Assembly that he backed the idea of a decree or law to fight corruption.

-- An official from the Washington-based International Food Policy Research Institute says Vietnam could surpass even Thailand in becoming the world's largest exporter of rice with better marketing and export promotion even if the country grew less rice than it has in recent harvests.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, meeting members of the ASEAN Confederation of Journalists, called for greater cooperation to prevent inaccurate information within the region.

-- Vietnam's Minister for Labour, War invalids and Social Welfare Tran Dinh Hoan told the National Assembly that the current wages policy has left many with unreasonable and unfair incomes and the problem ought to be addressed in 1997.

-- Vietnam sold 27 billion dong ($2.44 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 7.89 percent to domestic institution at an auction on Wednesday. The Finance Ministry had originaly expected to sell 70 billion dong worth of notes.
